claims.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
claims.evidence: Let L be the number of feature occurrences. Every no-teleport transition has a nonempty live common-feature set and deletes both endpoint occurrences of each such feature, so it decreases the live-occurrence count by at least two. Any solution therefore has at most floor(L/2) transitions. Its tile sequence is polynomial length, and an explicit verifier can check distinct consecutive tiles, compute and delete exactly all live common features, reject empty intersections, and finally require an empty live set. This proves NP membership.
claims.search_method: Direct certificate-length and verifier proof, supplemented by exact exhaustive certificate checks on the finite test families.

claims.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
claims.evidence: Necessity: the moves deleting a feature f pair all vertices of its support S_f, producing a perfect matching M_f. Every move belongs to at least one such matching, and an unordered tile pair cannot recur because its first traversal deletes every then-live common feature. Thus the solution is an Euler trail of the simple union H. A nonmatching H-edge between two f-vertices can occur only after at least one endpoint's f-matching edge. Sufficiency: simulate an Euler order satisfying that precedence rule and suppose the earliest matching edge m_f(u)=uv that fails has f previously deleted at u by uw. Edge uw is nonmatching for f. Since uv is later, precedence forces m_f(w) before uw. By global earliestness, m_f(w) successfully deleted f at w, so uw could not have deleted f at u, a contradiction. Hence every matching edge deletes its intended feature; every H-edge is legal because it belongs to a matching; and all occurrences are deleted.
claims.search_method: Independent proof of both directions and exhaustive comparison of the characterization with raw game search on 2,832 exact finite cases, including supports of size six.

claims.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
claims.evidence: A feature with support {u,v} can be deleted only on transition uv. Collapsing all features with the same endpoint pair gives a simple graph K. Every solution must traverse every K-edge, every legal transition is a K-edge, and no K-edge can be used twice after its first traversal clears all features on that pair. Solutions are therefore exactly Euler trails of K. Conversely, an Euler trail is legal and clears every associated feature. Connectivity of the edge-bearing vertices and zero or two odd degrees decide existence. Endpoint extraction, integer-pair radix sorting and deduplication, followed by connectivity and parity scans, take linear time in the standard indexed word-RAM representation; repeated features on one pair do not affect this bound.
claims.search_method: Direct reduction to the simple endpoint graph, checked exhaustively on all 1,099 labeled simple graphs through five vertices and all 729 multiplicity-0/1/2 assignments on the six endpoint pairs of four vertices.

claims.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
claims.evidence: For supports {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,1,2,3}, and {0,1,2,4}, choose matchings 01, 02, 12, (03,12), and (04,12). Their simple union is {01,02,12,03,04}, with Euler trail 3-0-1-2-0-4. Nevertheless no solution exists. The first three features force the core triangle. Tiles 3 and 4 must be trail endpoints, attached to core vertices i and j. If i differs from j, the move graph has four odd vertices; hence i=j. Starting at 3, after 3i the triangle must be traversed as a circuit at i before the final i4. Its first edge from i deletes at i the feature supported on {0,1,2,4}, making i4 illegal. Reversing the trail gives the symmetric contradiction. Exact search independently found all 95 reachable states unsolved.
claims.search_method: Analytic parity and temporal case split, plus exhaustive exact state search and mechanical validation of every displayed matching and Euler-trail edge.

claims.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
claims.evidence: A state (v,M), with current tile v and L-bit live-occurrence mask M, determines all future legal moves. For each w distinct from v, scanning the incidence data identifies exactly the features live at both endpoints; an empty set forbids the move, while otherwise all corresponding endpoint bits are cleared. Every transition decreases |M| by at least two, so induction on |M| proves the acyclic reachability recurrence exact. There are at most n·2^L states and O(nL) work per state, yielding O(n^2 L·2^L) time. A directly indexed memo table uses O(n·2^L) space and is shared across all starting tiles.
claims.search_method: Independent recurrence and asymptotic analysis; exact occurrence-mask dynamic programming was compared with a separately represented raw breadth-first search throughout the 2,832-case general test suite.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a complete complexity classification for arbitrary sharing number by either a polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness result. The draft establishes NP membership, an exact but non-polynomial characterization, a special-case linear algorithm, a counterexample to a static relaxation, and an exponential exact algorithm. These are correct and material, but they provide neither requested unrestricted classification result. The final writeup explicitly says that the target remains unresolved and labels the contribution PARTIAL, so it does not overclaim; claimed_resolution is therefore ACCURATE.
checks_performed: Read only the designated source JSON and draft JSON as external inputs; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior frontier output, verification report, or other solution.

Independently derived the certificate bound, both directions of the ordered-matching characterization, the frequency-two reduction, the five-tile impossibility proof, and the state-space recurrence and bounds.

Created and ran the exact-integer checker at /tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/fun2026_tiles_no_teleport_general/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/audit_exact_check.py; SHA-256 7a56d7bc50300c9493c1b425d4c0382c2eae21e93c2394c1d12c7442082a436c.

The checker passed 2,832 general characterization/solver cases, covering all feature multisets of up to three features through four tiles, all multisets of up to two features on five tiles, additional even-support families through six tiles, 62,280 raw reachable states, and 40,020 memoized occurrence-mask states.

The checker also passed all 1,099 labeled simple graphs through five vertices, all 729 multiplicity-0/1/2 frequency-two instances on four vertices, and the five-tile obstruction; the obstruction had 95 reachable states and 380 examined transitions while its static union admitted trail 3-0-1-2-0-4.
All finite decisions used integer masks and exhaustive enumeration; no floating-point decision was used.
